title: Example — replace with a theory, in your own words
summary: One or two sentences summarising the claim. Entries with "example": true are ignored. "video" and "timestamp" are only for your own reference and are never published.
basis: What in-game material the claim rests on.

title: Abraxas is the being beyond every pair of opposites
summary: The name is taken unchanged from the Gnostic Abraxas, a god above good and evil, creation and destruction. He reads Abby's two eye colours (space and time in WuWa's colour code) as a sign that the entity sits above both, not just on them.
basis: The real Gnostic name; Abby's eye colours.

title: Attributes are habits of one pure frequency, not separate powers
summary: Everything is one underlying frequency since the Lament rewrote reality into waves. The six attributes are only tendencies in how a Resonator shapes it (Spectro leans to time, Aero to space), so any attribute can touch any domain, just less efficiently. Beings that command the raw frequency act on concepts such as creation and destruction.
basis: The game's premise that the world is frequency; attribute flavour.

title: Somnoire is a “Cradle of Eternity” built to hold endless things
summary: Dreams and hope have a beginning but no end, which he calls Eternity. Somnoire was built as a container that copies that concept, which is why it can hold Eternity at all; it is not stronger than what it seals, only shaped like it.
basis: The “Cradle of Eternity” naming inside Somnoire.

title: Denia is the “Cradle of Void”, and the blue Denia is the real one
summary: A cradle must stay true to the concept it holds, so the hopeless, blue form of Denia is the true vessel of the Void, and her hopeful side keeps sliding back. He reads her as a Fractsidus trial run at making a Threnodian Resonator for Aleph-1.
basis: The “Cradle of Void” item from Denia's boss and her story arc.

title: The “White Tower” is an Eternity entity sealed by a matching concept
summary: “White Tower” is only what the ruined civilisation called it. It devours hope, slipped into Somnoire to feed on the dreams stored there, and was sealed because Somnoire is built on the same concept — the way comics seal higher beings with a conceptual twin rather than a stronger weapon.
basis: The Somnoire story of the two cats and the White Tower; Dreaming Deep text about its endless hunger.

title: Somnoire's makers may have trapped the White Tower on purpose
summary: The cats say the White Tower got in by accident, but the black cat didn't want to help that civilisation and the white cat insisted. He suspects whoever ordered the cats planned the trap from the start.
basis: The cats' differing attitudes in the story and trailer.

title: Abby was born when Rover defeated Dreamless
summary: Dreamless was a Threnodian vessel fuelled by the dreams of fallen soldiers and Jinzhou's hope for victory, so it carried Eternity-type frequency and tore a hole into Somnoire. Its “bring back to the mother” line was it sensing that frequency in Rover. Absorbing Dreamless gave Rover enough of it for Abby to manifest.
basis: Dreamless's dialogue; the Somnoire leak in the 1.x story.

title: Rover is a “Resonator of Abraxas” project
summary: Abby's frequency was inside Rover long before 1.0 (per Shorekeeper), so Rover was built — by the Somnoire makers and the goddess of the opening — to resonate with Abraxas, remade from pure gold Remnant each loop until it finally worked in this timeline.
basis: Shorekeeper's remark that Abby resonated with Rover long ago; Rover's gold Remnant.

title: Abby, not Rover alone, is what breaks the loop
summary: A Möbius-strip loop is escaped either by cutting the strip or by adding something from outside it. Abby is that outside element, which is why this timeline is the special one; he disagrees with calling Rover alone “the one who brings change”.
basis: The game's loop/iteration hints; the trailer's “new possibility” line.

title: Hiyuki can borrow the timeline where she succeeded
summary: Her power finds a version of herself that succeeded, takes that timeline and absorbs it as a power-up. The Grand Architect wanted her as a Threnodian Resonator for that reason, and she refused.
basis: His reading of Hiyuki's story.

title: The White Tower is only Abraxas's “beginning” half
summary: Gold stands for time and Eternity, blue for space and destruction. What is sealed in Somnoire is the Eternity half of Abraxas; the “ending” half — the Lament and the Threnodians — is still loose, which is why Solaris has endings without a beginning.
basis: Gold/blue colour symbolism in the trailer weapons.

title: Tacetite weapons cost ordinary people their lifespan
summary: Low-rarity Tacetite weapons let non-Resonators hurt Lament creatures, but using one shortens their life. Resonators carry weapons anyway to channel frequency efficiently and keep Overclocking in check.
basis: Weapon rarity tiers and Tacetite descriptions.

title: Threnodians can't die; only their vessels can
summary: Threnodians are concepts, so what Rover fights are the vessels they take, like Dreamless. Defeating a vessel doesn't end the Threnodian.
basis: The vessel framing around Dreamless and other Threnodian fights.

title: The New Federation will run on frequency gadgets
summary: Resonators are outcast there, so ordinary people will buy Tacetite-core suits and weapons to match them, including disposable frequency weapons that explode when pushed past their limit.
basis: A prediction from the New Federation's anti-Resonator setting.

title: Each Overseer is fused with a Calamity-class Tacet Discord
summary: Overseers are a Fractsidus project to combine a Resonator with a Calamity-class Tacet Discord, so every Overseer has one of their own.
basis: Overseer boss fights and Fractsidus experiments.

title: Higher entities engineered the whole tragedy
summary: After the Solaris arc he expects a twist: cosmic “observers” who set up Somnoire, the White Tower disaster and Rover on purpose — possibly with the Grand Architect as one of their agents.
basis: Story-structure expectation; no direct evidence.

title: Exploring Somnoire is what grows Abby
summary: Rover is the only “Dream Walker” given proper access, and each dreamscape explored lets Rover and Abby resonate with more of the frequency stored there, so the Somnoire events are leveling Abby up rather than filler.
basis: Rover's Dream Walker role in Somnoire events.

title: Abby's trailer voice mixes animal, pulsar and black-hole sounds
summary: He hears three layers in the voice: an animal sound for the mythic beast, a pulsar recording, and the low rumble of the TON 618 black hole — sound design that marks Abby as a cosmic, Abraxas-level being.
basis: His listening of the Transcendo trailer's sound design (unconfirmed).

title: “Astral Modulator” means converting frequency between analog and digital
summary: Like a modem, Rover's title is about turning natural (analog) frequency into the digital form the Tethys System runs on and back, with the piano as the anchor instrument.
basis: Rover's Astral Modulator title; Tethys System lore.

title: Today's Solaris is a “Plan 3” world living inside the old one
summary: The current world is a stop-gap world anchored by Shorekeeper inside the original, Lament-eaten world. Lament outbreaks are leaks from that original world, and Fractsidus's “True Lament” means tearing Plan 3 open until it falls back into the original. He places the Grand Architect as someone from that original world.
basis: In-game Tethys and Plan 3 material; Fractsidus's “True Lament” wording.

title: Solaris orbits a broken three-star system
summary: The trailer shows a stable three-star orbit like Alpha Centauri; he thinks one star (an “Instance”) collapsed into a black hole and threw the system into the chaotic eras of Liu Cixin's Three-Body Problem, which he says WuWa's eras and Dark Forest names borrow from. Fractsidus, the “fractured star”, may serve that collapsed star, and Tethys data listing Instance One as “(Solar)” would mean its authority passed back to the main star.
basis: Trailer orbit imagery; Tethys data entries; Dreaming Deep's redshift/blueshift scenes.

title: The trailer's emblems point to Fractsidus's New Federation cast
summary: He reads Overseer insignia for a Zashiki-warashi, Balanophora, Eris and a nine-headed Hydra, and predicts Hydra experimenting on outcast Resonators living in a sunken oasis city, with Phrolova and others backing the main antagonists.
basis: Emblems in the Transcendo trailer; predictions.

title: Weapon cores change colour as they take on the wielder's frequency
summary: Pure Remnant/Tacetite is gold, as seen in low-rarity weapons. Signature weapons' cores have absorbed their owner's frequency and turned other colours — Augusta's sun-red, Iuno's — so the core colour shows whose weapon it is.
basis: Visible core colours on in-game weapon models.

title: Threnodians are the true gods; Sentinels are made to counter them
summary: Threnodians arise naturally from disaster, so they are the native “gods” of this cosmology. Sentinels are engines civilisations built with god-like authority to stand against them.
basis: Sentinels described as Oracle Engines; Threnodians born from the Laments.

title: Abby is the part of Abraxas let out by a deal with the cat
summary: The giant cat with Abby-like eyes is the original Somnoire cat after ages of its frequency fusing with the sealed Abraxas. Their deal let a pure fragment of Abraxas's frequency out — Abby — while the rest stays sealed. Abby guards hope where Abraxas devours it, which he expects to collide when Abraxas is freed.
basis: The cat's look in the Transcendo trailer; the deal it mentions.

title: Leviathan's power breaches Somnoire
summary: Leviathan turns imagination into reality, which punctures Somnoire. That explains Nightmare Tacet Discords in Septimont, and how Fractsidus moved Scar out of Mingting's prison through Somnoire. Their larger aim would be to unseal Abraxas, which he sees as suicidal.
basis: Nightmare enemies in Rinascita; Scar's escape; Leviathan's powers.

title: Somnoire's outer layers exist to hide its deepest one
summary: The film festival deep inside Somnoire invited Rover by name, so all of Somnoire is tied to Rover. The gatekeepers' shallow layer and the unknown “deep water” zone may be there to cover the deepest layer, where the old civilisation's records are kept; Dorothy likely lives in the deep-water zone.
basis: The festival's personal invitation; the gatekeepers' account of what they can and can't reach.

title: The film festival is a crime scene, and Rover is the detective
summary: The festival's true ending calls Somnoire's depths the tombstone of D's lost civilisation, rebuilt from memory as films. Because each film plays out through the viewer's choices, he thinks D is gathering evidence for Rover to find who destroyed that civilisation — possibly the Threnodian called the White Tower.
basis: The festival's true ending; D's lines about detectives, culprits and evidence.

title: The lost civilisation fought Threnodians and built satellites
summary: Details about the festival's film crew suggest the civilisation behind them could stand up to a Threnodian, explore beyond the planet and put artificial satellites in orbit — more than anyone has managed since the Lament.
basis: Easter eggs about the crew in the festival events.

title: The White Tower began as a world-saving hero
summary: All four earlier films retell Rover's adventures as saviour-hero stories, and the White Tower is only named in the fifth. The true-ending bosses — a Hecate, a “betrayer”, and a Nightmare version of a hero's banner — hint that a hero who wanted to save the world turned into the disaster.
basis: The festival's hero theme and its boss line-up.

title: Dorothy remembers a future Rover because Somnoire's doors cross time
summary: Dorothy says she will help Rover “as usual” and that it happened “sometime in the future”. Just as present-day Rover saved Aemeath as a child in 3.1, Somnoire's doors may let visitors from different times in, so Dorothy met a later Rover first; neither of them is misremembering.
basis: Dorothy's 2.2 dialogue; the 3.1 scene where Rover saves the young Aemeath.

title: Dorothy is a real resident of the dream, kept alive by it
summary: The black cat sent Dorothy back into Somnoire because staying outside too long harms her, so the dream's frequency likely sustains her. She has friends, learns songs and lives her own life even when Rover isn't there.
basis: The 2.2 event's ending; how other characters describe her.

title: Somnoire lets people from different eras work together against the Lament
summary: Residents' thoughts reshape the dream, so it can grow its own history. Combined with doors that cross time, Somnoire becomes a meeting place where people who never shared an era can pass discoveries to one another; the white cat keeping secrets for a past Rover hints Rover is already part of it.
basis: The 3.4 note on Dream Abodes; the white cat's comments about the past Rover.

title: The black gatekeeper rebelled after seeing itself in the dreams
summary: Its job was deleting dreams that couldn't help against the Lament. Over time it came to value the lives inside them, realised it was no different from them, stopped filtering and opened more doors — which let Somnoire spill into reality in 1.4.
basis: The 1.4 Somnoire storyline.

title: Quotation marks give away an impostor
summary: In Somnoire stories, a name shown in quotation marks is someone in disguise: the black sheep in 1.2 and “Dorothy” in 1.3 were the black gatekeeper, and the “Dorothy” in 3.3 gained quotation marks the moment she was exposed.
basis: Speaker names in the 1.2, 1.3 and 3.3 Somnoire events.

title: Somnoire was built by the lost civilisation
summary: The gatekeepers call Somnoire's creators “they”: closely tied to Rover but not Rover. A professor in 1.0 calls “them” our past and our future, and Shorekeeper's texts use the same word for the old civilisation.
basis: Gatekeeper dialogue in 1.4; a 1.0 professor's line; Shorekeeper's texts.

title: Aleph-1's arrival was the fifth Global Lament, less than a thousand years ago
summary: Waveworn Phenomena tied to black holes belong to Aleph-1, and so far there are three: Lahai-Roi, the Port City of Guixu and Honami. They date from under a thousand years ago, and the damage stayed partial because the Exostrider sealed Aleph-1 before it fully entered Solaris.
basis: Lament records and the types of Waveworn Phenomenon in each region.

title: Rover's vision near Dreamless was Rover hearing the world
summary: “I may have resonated with the Tacet Discord” is Rover reading the world's frequencies, much like Yangyang does. The vision came as Phrolova stirred the Dreamless cocoon and Abby, hungry for that frequency, picked it up.
basis: Rover's dialogue in the 1.0 frontline quest.

title: A destroyed Tacet Discord's frequency regathers into a stronger one
summary: When a core breaks, its scattered reverberation searches for a new vessel, reunites and evolves into a higher-class Tacet Discord. Phrolova can steer these loose frequencies into vessels on purpose.
basis: Reverberation lore and Phrolova's abilities in the 1.0 story.

title: Scar staged the Qichi Village tragedy to manipulate Rover
summary: Scar's “wolf and sheep” story is built on a tragedy Fractsidus prepared in advance, and it is told so that every reading leads somewhere useful to them: a newly awakened Rover either blames themself or concludes the world is unfair and everyone should be equal to gods.
basis: Scar's dialogue and the dialogue choices in the Qichi Village quest.

title: Fractsidus's promised last Threnodian echoes the Dajjal
summary: Fractsidus waits for a promised being that can make anything real and topple the divine order. He compares this to the Dajjal of Islamic eschatology, and reads Scar's shepherd story the same way.
basis: Fractsidus's “promise” dialogue; a religious comparison of his own.

title: Qichi Village turning on the gifted child mirrors Europe's witch hunts
summary: After the disaster the villagers blamed the one child with unusual powers, the way people in early modern Europe blamed anyone with unusual knowledge for plagues and misfortune.
basis: The child's story in the Qichi Village quest.

title: Fractsidus's hatred of humanity was learned in the New Federation
summary: Many members come from the New Federation's Lawless Zone, where Resonators are outcast. Living there taught them that people are cruel and undeserving, and that experience shapes the group's ideology.
basis: New Federation lore on Resonator discrimination; members' backgrounds.

title: Scar and Rover are both black sheep, and the ending will judge them
summary: Both defy fate. Fractsidus does it by trying to make people into gods and overturn the divine order, Rover by helping each civilisation choose its own path. He thinks Scar's question returns at the end of Rover's journey — and points out the irony that Fractsidus becomes the shepherd it hates, sacrificing Rinascita's people for its research.
basis: The black sheep story and its three dialogue options; Fractsidus's actions in Rinascita.

title: Changli orchestrated the 1.0 token trail
summary: The tokens Jinhsi handed Rover were placed to teach Rover what Fractsidus is, with Sanhua watching and the Black Shores feeding information. Fractsidus's later attempt to infiltrate Jinzhou through Rover walked into another of Changli's traps.
basis: Scar's remark that Jinhsi was leaving clues; how the 1.0 quests are sequenced.

title: The time loop has been set up since 1.0
summary: Nothing about the loop in the new trailer is new. Professor Heisen's “they are our past and our future” and his plea to “the person from the past who is the future” already pointed at Rover in 1.0, and 1.3 repeated it everywhere on the Black Shores: “the past is the future, the start is the end”, even in a robot's hex-code line.
basis: Professor Heisen's 1.0 dialogue; repeated Black Shores lines in 1.3; Rover's first memory of arriving there: “this world has not begun, yet we have already seen its end.”

title: The Goddess holds time, the Shorekeeper holds space
summary: Resolution K-626 is read as naming two powers made by the lost civilisation: the first, controlling time, is the Goddess from the opening cinematic; the second, controlling space, is the Shorekeeper.
basis: Wording of the K-626 resolution document in 1.3; the Goddess and Rover's origin linked in the 1.0 ruins.

title: Somnoire's two gatekeepers must stay balanced, and they serve a master
summary: From 1.0 to 1.4 the black gatekeeper went rogue and was corrected, with a warning that the white one might act next; later the white one did, and in 3.6 let slip that they have a master. Somnoire's text also says three times that time is a circle, “a memory of the future”.
basis: Dialogue across the recurring Somnoire events; the 3.6 slip about a master.

title: The Chapter 1 ruins lab and Fractsidus ran the same experiment
summary: The ruins researchers, failing to recreate the miracle they once saw, built a copy of the god's form instead: specimen A038, a mechanical Tacet Discord. That is exactly Fractsidus's line of work (fusing Tacet Discords with human bodies), and the lab was funded by a Fractsidus Overseer. Scar's second form may be its result.
basis: Research notes in the Chapter 1 ruins; the boss's description; the Overseer funding mentioned there.

title: Two futures: humanity becomes the Goddess, or the Lament makes her
summary: Either future humans ascend into something like the Goddess and send Rover back to fix a timeline that is going wrong, or the “god” is what the True Lament leaves behind: every human mind merged into Threnodian bodies, on a broken world like the shattered moon in the trailer. Then the future itself is what is being prevented.
basis: Heisen's “they are our past and our future”; the ruins notes calling their copy a false gate; Scar's speech about the Lament; Rover recurring at Jinzhou's disasters (Aalto: this is not the first awakening).

title: Rover came from a future star system, not from Solaris
summary: Rover is neither from Solaris nor from the lost civilisation, but from a distant system Solaris has not yet reached. Unable to go home, Rover lived on Solaris until it became a second home, then crossed time again to save it.
basis: Rover's Lahai-Roi lines about a distant home, a duty and no way back; the early concept trailer's pod launch scene.

title: The trailer's star map imitates the Voyager Golden Record
summary: The rings-and-dots chart reads like the Golden Record's pulsar map: coordinates and a recognisable signal for whoever finds them. Lahai-Roi says Solaris launched nine probes before the Etheric Sea closed (nine stars on the Spacetrek emblem), and the game's hero is literally named the Wanderer, a Voyager.
basis: Visual match with the Golden Record cover; the nine-probe account in Lahai-Roi.

title: Rover is a sealed seed of a whole civilisation
summary: The amber Rover floating in the pod is frozen time, a time capsule. Rover's first power is time-related because that freezing is what Rover is made of; it carries another civilisation's knowledge forward, like the Fire Seed plan in The Three-Body Problem.
basis: The amber/pod imagery; the pod already seen in the 2023 relaunch and earliest concept trailers.

title: Tacetite printed a new Rover
summary: The pod came out of Tacetite, which 1.3 showed can both absorb and record frequencies and release them to rebuild living matter. So the Rover we play may be a reprint made after the stone had absorbed the original Rover and pod; the trailer flashes cell division and a human body plan right there.
basis: 1.3's two uses of Tacetite; cell and body diagrams flashed during the pod sequence.

title: Everyone who lands on Solaris is remade as human
summary: A 2.0 line says the New Federation has many aliens, yet they look like ordinary Solarians. If Tacetite reshapes whatever arrives, every visitor ends up in human form, Rover included.
basis: 2.0 NPC remark about aliens in the New Federation; the Tacetite reprint reading of the trailer.

title: The White Tower wakes on a schedule and eats bright civilisations
summary: The festival's final case says civilisations shone so brightly that they drew the White Tower's gaze, and it reached out on instinct; “civilisations”, plural. Researchers in “Gift from the Sky” wished they had studied it centuries earlier, so it sleeps and wakes on a known cycle. The trailer's countdown and clock-hand spikes are that cycle.
basis: Somnoire film festival final case; the “Gift from the Sky” encounter; the clock imagery in the trailer.

title: The Moon was an artificial satellite, shattered by a cosmic Threnodian
summary: The cycle of catastrophes predates the Moon, which a previous civilisation built. A cosmic Threnodian broke it; that is when Waveworn and Tacet Discords began, and the Etheric Sea closed over Solaris both as cage and shield. The moons seen today are phantoms of a moon long gone.
basis: Moon item text: the moon shattered long ago and what is seen is a past phantom; Threnodian imagery tied to moons.

title: Order to chaos: the trailer's spikes match Mortefi's and Calcharo's scans
summary: The spikes on Solaris turn from symmetric to irregular after the cosmic Threnodian's jump. That mirrors two in-game reports: Mortefi's stable Resonator wave is a regular sawtooth, Calcharo's is the same shape but disordered. Before the Threnodian, frequency was orderly; Waveworn is the disorder.
basis: Mortefi and Calcharo Resonator reports; the trailer's spike sequence.

title: Solaris sits in a gravity well, near a black hole
summary: A gravity-well diagram on a screen, plus a 1.3 line calling gravity the old era's last truth, suggests Solaris is not in normal space and that something used gravity to lock onto its system.
basis: The gravity-well screen in the trailer; the 1.3 line about gravity.

title: Tethys is five parts on paired orbits, with a hidden top authority
summary: Around the First Instance run two orbits of opposed pairs: a Sentinel prototype (looking like Jué) with the Fallacy of No Return, and the Shorekeeper with a new character. That new figure would be the unnamed system in K-626 with the highest authority on the Black Shores, the base code that overruled Rover and keeps Tethys on the survival path.
basis: Trailer staging of the Tethys system; K-626's unnamed co-deciding system; the scene where Tethys overrules Rover.

title: Rover wiped their own memory and had themself re-dropped
summary: The full pre-amnesia timeline: home destroyed, Aleph-1, buried on Solaris, dug up by the lost civilisation, first Lament, Huanglong founded, the Black Shores and Sentinels made, the Moon built and broken, the Etheric Sea. Unable to win, Rover erased their memory and used the time-controlling First Instance to send themself back in as one of Solaris's own.
basis: Sequence of the trailer read chronologically; pod imagery after the First Instance's light shatters.

title: Fractsidus raided the Black Shores with inside help
summary: Five Overseers, Phrolova among them, push all the way to the Black Shores and may strike the Shorekeeper. Since only members know where the Black Shores are, someone opened the door: possibly the hidden survival system, after the Black Shores began studying Threnodian Resonators (Aalto, 2.7). Or Fractsidus came through Somnoire.
basis: Overseer emblems in the trailer; 1.3 on the Black Shores' secret location; Aalto's 2.7 remark.

title: Somnoire's rewinding doors reach Earth, and the players are Rover's anchor
summary: As doors close the trailer rewinds through a masked-hero city, dinosaurs and ancient sea life. Either Somnoire draws on the whole planet's collective memory, or it crosses the fourth wall into our Earth, like Lem's Solaris surfacing the visitors' memories. Then we, from Earth, are the new variable Rover was looking for.
basis: The door sequence after the concept-art card; the link to Lem's novel.

title: The festival's masked-hero city was a real past civilisation
summary: One film-festival story has a people who knew nothing of frequencies, thought they had superpowers, and turned into masked fighters against monsters when the Lament came, much like a Kamen Rider show. It ended in ruin; the festival films may be records of real lost civilisations.
basis: The festival script; the same city appearing behind a Somnoire door in the trailer.

title: The new white cat is the festival's director, M
summary: The cat at Somnoire's core has been seen before as “M”: the director credited in the April Fools animation, and the reviewer behind a festival map-report review. It may be the partner the black gatekeeper mentioned, tied to Abby rather than Rover, and is said to have tempted the Shorekeeper (“never trade with dreams”). Version 4.0 should tell Abby's origin.
basis: April Fools animation credits; a Somnoire exploration-report review; the Shorekeeper's affinity story opening line.
